The preserved-copy feature is in. Refresh **http://maker:4001** and let's confirm it:

**1. Every link keeps a copy.** Each card now shows a small green **"📄 Saved copy"** flag, meaning a copy of the page was preserved when you saved it.

**2. View the preserved copy.** On any card, click **"📄 View saved copy."** A reader opens showing the page's preserved content, with a header stating **"Preserved copy · captured [date]"** and a clear banner reminding you this is your saved copy, *not* the live page.

**3. The reassurance.** This copy stays in your library regardless of what happens to the original — so even if the source site changes the article or goes offline entirely, your saved version remains readable. (Contrast with clicking the **title**, which still goes to the live original.)

**4. New saves too.** Add a new link and it also gets a preserved copy, captured at the moment you saved it.

Two things to confirm:

- **A copy is captured automatically for every link at save time** — you don't have to ask for it. My assumption is that "always preserve" matches your wish to never lose something. (I've noted for later that automatic capture has practical trade-offs around storage and pages behind logins — we can revisit depth of capture separately.) Does automatic-for-everything feel right?
- The preserved copy captures the page's **readable content** (text and structure) as of when you saved it — enough to revisit what mattered — rather than a pixel-perfect photograph of the page. Is preserving the readable content what you're after?

Give the saved copy a look and tell me if this delivers the "won't lose it" reassurance you wanted.
